summary_exact_relevant_lines.text: **Map A bonuses:** its seven support-token bonuses, from top to bottom, are snap one display card, build a size-2 standard enclosure free, gain five money, gain one conservation, gain two reputation, gain twelve money and gain three X-tokens. The first four are received immediately when uncovered and again as break income; the last three are one-time. Take a chosen bonus before or after its project's reward. On Map A the second partner zoo upgrades a card, the third hires a worker and the fourth grants two conservation. The second university upgrades a card and the third grants two conservation. Other maps use their printed bonuses.
- **Conservation project work (strength 5):** choose either to support a conservation project already in play, or to play a Conservation Project card from your hand and support it immediately.

- **New-card sources:** use your hand. With Association II, you may instead use a display card within reputation range and pay its folder number as an additional cost; do not replenish the display until turn end.
- **Enter play:** put the new card on the leftmost space above the Association board; push existing cards one place right.

- **Overflow:** depending on player count there can be up to 2, 3, or 4 cards above the board (e.g., 3 with three players). If the new card exceeds the limit, discard the rightmost card. Return its player tokens to their owners' supplies, not to their zoo maps; their map bonuses stay activated.
- **Base Conservation Projects:** the projects below the board never move and are never replenished, even when fully supported.

- **Two separate support limits:** a reward level is available only if **no player at all** has a token on it. Each level can hold **one token total across all players**. Separately, you normally may support a particular project only once, even if another level is free. Thus an opponent's token blocks that level too; having no token of your own on the level is insufficient.

1. **Fulfill the chosen condition printed on the card**, and choose a reward level that has no player token on it. If you fulfill several conditions, choose one. You may support each project only once, never one already holding your token.
2. Take one player token of your choice from the left edge of your zoo map and put it on the chosen condition.
3. Gain the depicted conservation reward and any depicted reputation. Removing the map token activates its uncovered bonus: take it immediately, before or after the project reward at your choice.
4. **Recurring bonus:** if the uncovered map bonus is marked as recurring income, gain that same bonus again in every break.
- **Discarded conservation projects:** tokens on a project card pushed off the display return to the owners' **supply**, not to the bonus spaces on their zoo maps (the bonuses stay activated).

clauses.proposition: A new project may be played only together with immediate support.
clauses.question_wording: How may a Conservation Project enter play
clauses.reason: The permissible way to introduce a project includes its mandatory immediate support; merely placing a card is not the permitted entry.

clauses.proposition: The new card may come from hand.
clauses.question_wording: How may a Conservation Project enter play

clauses.question_wording: How may a Conservation Project enter play

clauses.question_wording: How may a Conservation Project enter play
clauses.reason: This cost is a condition of the permitted display-entry route, so omitting it leaves that route incompletely specified.

clauses.proposition: A display project must be within reputation range.
clauses.question_wording: How may a Conservation Project enter play
clauses.reason: The range restriction determines which display projects can enter through that route.

clauses.proposition: Move existing above-board projects one position right.

clauses.reason: This is the placement procedure that determines which project becomes overflowing. The broad entry/overflow wording fairly includes it without naming each movement.

clauses.proposition: The above-board row holds at most two/three/four projects with two/three/four players.
clauses.reason: A usable explanation of overflow includes the row capacity that determines when it occurs.

clauses.proposition: Discard the rightmost project when entry exceeds the row capacity.
clauses.reason: Directly answers which overflowing project leaves play and what happens to it.

clauses.proposition: Return tokens on the discarded project to their owners’ supplies.
clauses.reason: Directly answers the destination of tokens on the overflowing project.

clauses.proposition: Those tokens do not return to the owners’ zoo maps.
clauses.reason: This is a negative clarification of the required token destination, rather than a separate additional rule. It can be satisfied by an unambiguous statement that the tokens return to supply.

clauses.proposition: Base projects below the board never shift.
clauses.reason: The question asks entry and overflow, not the persistence of the separate base row. Restricting the required movement/overflow procedure to projects above the board answers it without separately asserting that base projects never move.

clauses.reason: No wording asks about replenishment of base projects or what happens when a base project is fully supported; this is accurate neighboring context.

clauses.reason: An unoccupied reward level is an eligibility condition for support. The occupancy condition applies across all players.

clauses.proposition: The player must fulfill the chosen printed condition.
clauses.reason: Directly answers what condition must be met to support the chosen level.

clauses.proposition: Normally each player may support a given project only once.
clauses.reason: The question explicitly asks once limits; this is the ordinary project-per-player limit in the fixed key.

clauses.reason: The source question asks where the token comes from. It does not ask whether the player may choose among source tokens; the source can be answered completely without that freedom-of-choice detail.

Mentioning project rewards as the reference point for before/after bonus timing does not require specifying the track awards.

final_required_part_list.part: Introduce a new project only while immediately supporting it.
Use a hand card, or with Association II use an in-range display card and pay its folder number.
Put the new project leftmost above the Association board and shift the existing above-board row right.
The above-board capacity is the player count (2/3/4); discard the rightmost excess card.
Return tokens on the discarded project to their owners’ supplies, not their maps; the negative clarification is the same destination requirement.
Support a fulfilled printed condition at a level unoccupied by any player’s token.
Normally each player can support each project only once.
Take the support token from the left edge of the player’s zoo map.
Receive the uncovered bonus immediately, before or after the project reward at the player’s choice.
If marked as recurring income, receive the uncovered bonus again at each break.
